headline: Astronomers watch a giant star swallow its neighbor
pages: Astronomers have watched a giant star in the Andromeda Galaxy spend nearly a decade swallowing a much smaller companion before an eruption in late 2025, according to a new Nature study. The giant is about seven times the mass of the Sun. The process, called common envelope evolution, was proposed in the 1970s to explain how some very tight pairs of stars form, but no one had seen it happen. When an aging star swells, it can engulf its companion; the two then share a loosely bound envelope of gas, and the swallowed star loses orbital energy and spirals inward.

A team led by Viraj Karambelkar of Columbia University found the system while searching Andromeda for stars that change in brightness, using the WINTER telescope at Palomar Observatory and NASA NEOWISE data. One giant had been brightening for seven years. Karambelkar said the event lasts a few years to a few decades, a blip on cosmic time scales. Source: Ars Technica.
